title: Wix Review (2026)
intro: Wix is evaluated here as a website-first builder with integrated ecommerce — Wix is a website builder with integrated ecommerce. US annual tiles commonly published 2026: Light ~$17/mo (site, no store), Core ~$29/mo (accept payments / basic ecommerce), Business ~$39/mo, Business Elite ~$159/mo; monthly billing is higher. Free plan exists but does not unlock selling. Best for design-led SMBs that need a site and a store together — not a Shopify-class commerce OS. Pricing research 2026-08-18 from consistent first-party plan reporting; confirm live on wix.com/pricing. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s Ecommerce methodology (ease of use, storefront/commerce fit, catalog & order depth, checkout conversion, integrations, omnichannel/POS, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Wix when the website and brand pages are the product — and ecommerce is a first-class but secondary job on the same builder.
verdict: Choose Wix when the website and brand pages are the product — and ecommerce is a first-class but secondary job on the same builder. Consider Squarespace for design-led peers; Shopify for commerce-first SaaS; WooCommerce if you already live in WordPress. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, minimums and usage rates on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Drag-and-drop editor is the product strength — merchants launch sites without developers.
Primary job is website + store together; scored as website-builder commerce, not a full commerce OS.
Solid for SMB catalogs; weaker for complex B2B and multi-warehouse depth.
Payments unlock on Core+; conversion tooling exists but trails Shop Pay-class ecosystems.
App Market and native payments/channels cover SMB needs — not Magento-scale extensibility.
Limited retail POS story versus Square Online.
Business Elite helps, but high-GMV complex catalogs usually outgrow website-builder packaging.
Core/Business annual tiles are competitive for site+store SMBs when design speed matters.
Wix AI assists design and copy — useful, secondary to the builder job.

bestFor: SMBs that need a polished website and a store in one builder
Service businesses adding light product sales
Founders prioritizing design speed over commerce OS depth
notIdealFor: High-SKU catalogs, heavy B2B, or marketplace ops
Retailers whose center of gravity is POS hardware
Teams that need open-source code ownership
pros: Fast website + store launch for design-led SMBs
Clear ecommerce plan gate at Core
Integrated bookings/marketing for service + product mixes
cons: Not a Shopify peer for complex commerce ops
limitations: Website-builder commerce depth trails Shopify-class platforms on complex catalogs and B2B
Plan gates for selling start at Core — Free/Light are not store plans
Transaction/processing economics need a live TCO model at your GMV
Heavy customization can hit builder limits versus open-source stacks
pricingSummary: Ecommerce starts at Core ~$29/mo annual (~$36 monthly). Business $39, Business Elite $159 annual. Light $17 is site-only. Confirm live on wix.com/pricing.
whoShouldChoose: Choose Wix when the website and brand pages are the product — and ecommerce is a first-class but secondary job on the same builder.
whoShouldConsiderAlternatives: Consider Squarespace for design-led peers; Shopify for commerce-first SaaS; WooCommerce if you already live in WordPress.

faq.answer: Yes. Wix is evaluated as a website-first builder with integrated ecommerce.

faq.question: How is Wix priced?
faq.answer: Ecommerce starts at Core ~$29/mo annual (~$36 monthly). Business $39, Business Elite $159 annual. Light $17 is site-only. Confirm live on wix.com/pricing.

faq.question: Does Wix have a free plan or free trial?
faq.answer: Yes — a free plan is published. A free trial is documented. Confirm current terms with the vendor.

faq.question: Did SoftwareGlimpse personally test Wix?
faq.answer: No. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research evidence, not hands-on product usage. Affiliate relationships never influence scores.
